# KBD Constraints

Constraints the artifact-refiner QA gate validates for every change from
`phase-codex-plugin-distribution-and-ci` onward. Each completed change is checked
against these before archiving (`/refine-validate <change-id>`); a violation marks
the change BLOCKED.

## C-01 — Generated artifacts must be in sync

Any source consumed by a generator must have its generated outputs regenerated
and committed before the owning parent phase completes or its final phase
commit is pushed. A parent phase may name one later reconciliation change to batch this
work when several sibling changes edit the same generated surface; every earlier
change must identify that reconciliation change in persisted execution evidence,
and none may claim distribution certification in the interim. The reconciliation
change must run the generator twice, prove byte-identical tracked hashes, and run
the applicable drift validators before phase certification. A deferral that
crosses the parent-phase boundary, omits the named owner, or reaches parent-phase
certification, final commit, or push without regenerated outputs is a violation.

Also generator inputs, from the integration contract (v1.0.0) onward:
`shared/launchagents/*.plist` and `shared/systemd/*.service|.timer|.path` feed
`shared/services.manifest.json` via `scripts/generate-service-manifest.mjs`
(seam 3 of `docs/integration-contract.md`). Any change that edits, adds, or
deletes one of those templates MUST regenerate the manifest and pass
`npm run check:services-manifest` in the same change. The manifest is generated;
hand-editing it is a violation.

Specifically: after touching `.claude-plugin/*`, `.mcp.json`,
`hooks/hooks.json`, or `scripts/build-codex-plugin.js`, `npm run validate:codex`
MUST pass (no drift, valid manifest + marketplace) in the same change because
those files directly define the generator or already-generated plugin surface.
Hand-editing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` or
`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is always a violation — they are generated.

## C-02 — No committed secrets

No API keys, tokens, or passwords in tracked files. Env vars and `${VAR:-default}`
placeholders only; real secret values live in the environment or user-local config
(`~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.bash_profile`), never in the repo. Localhost dev
credentials that are already an established repo convention (e.g. surrealdb
`root/root`, the forge localhost dev token) are exempt.

## C-03 — Docs updated with surface changes

A change that alters the Codex plugin surface (manifest fields, marketplace
schema, MCP servers, hooks, install flow) must update `docs/codex-plugin.md` and,
where relevant, the CLAUDE.md "Codex CLI Integration" section in the same change.

## C-04 — Generators stay idempotent

`node scripts/build-codex-plugin.js` run twice must produce byte-identical output.
`--check` must exit non-zero on drift or invalid artifacts. New generator features
(e.g. source-type knobs) must preserve idempotency for a fixed input.

## C-05 — Scripts under launchd are bash 3.2 compatible

Any script that can be invoked by a launchd agent (macOS `/bin/bash` is 3.2) must
avoid `mapfile` / `declare -A`. Test with `/bin/bash script.sh`, not just `bash`.

## QA and local review coverage

Every change requires deterministic artifact validation followed by independent
cumulative diff review before archive and final certification, including small
and documentation-only changes. Missing tools or explicit skip flags record
`pending_review`; they do not imply a passing gate. Final certification requires
a completed review receipt or the explicit signed waiver required by the current
`kbd-execute` contract. Generated-output deferral is limited to C-01 above.

# Minimum completion plan — hard60-minute execution budget

## Outcome and feasibility

Aim: parent40/40 tasks,18/18changes; project338/338resolved (337complete+1cancelled),104/104changes, source on main and installed product/sites accepted. This is a conditional delivery target, not a guarantee. Two user merge windows, an exact mini memory-SHA approval, real Cortex input, successful acceptance are outside a guaranteed agent-only60minutes. If those are unavailable, preserve incomplete statuses and identify their exact owners. Never claim this plan itself completes production or resets the overdue parent cadence.

## Keep, reuse, stop

KEEP all completed functional source and reviewed documentation; no rollback without a demonstrated regression. KEEP existing real integration assertions and the no-live-home/no23001/local-only/signing/user-merge boundaries. KEEP existing coordinator only as a command reference where it works; do not redesign it.

REUSE successful evidence only for the exact unchanged input scope and environment: current production binaries, actual Companion process scenario, hook bytecode, rebase, report assembly, byte/mode materialization, unchanged distribution/partition/harness/version checks. Record hashes against existing receipts; if a relevant input changed, rerun only its affected check. Protected integrity runs against the eventual real committed candidate, not another new pseudo-release architecture.

STOP repeating all Cargo builds, scanning every worktree/content again, new harnesses, broad test suites, new CLI capabilities, live model benchmarking, repeated generation without changed inputs, full rebuilds prompted solely by metadata changes unrelated to binary behavior, and speculative helper fixes. # Why the release overran

The lead conflated complete functional source with release readiness, then treated a broad final verification contract as an instruction to engineer a new certification platform. The approved plan did require real integration evidence; inventing evidence would be wrong. The avoidable mistake was not decomposing that requirement into existing commands, reusable candidate-specific receipts, missing prerequisites, and human publication boundaries before execution.

The new coordinator combined build, scratch materialization, private commit construction, legacy scenarios, site serving, and content checks. Its own failures (Python syntax, digest formatting, omitted fixture tools/project identity, wrong candidate gitlink provenance) consumed subsequent cycles. Protected preparation lost stderr; another attempted fix was consequently speculative. The lead repeated source-done claims while release evidence was incomplete and continued beyond the cadence deadline instead of issuing a precise dependency report. This was process overreach and inaccurate communication, not justification for rewriting finished features.

Current facts: parent 16/18 changes and33/40 tasks complete; project98/104 changes,325 completed tasks,12 unfinished,1 cancelled. Cancelled reconcile-kbd-control-plane-projections/8 requires restarting sovereign-sync twice, explicitly superseded by the owner decision that it stay disabled in ordinary KBD. Target is338/338 resolved=337 complete+1 intentionally cancelled; never resurrect it to manipulate counts.

Latest affected batch21:57:59–22:20:17UTC took22m18s. Production CLI/hook/memory/prior-memory/Companion builds passed. Real Companion connected processes, hook-bytecode, rebase, research report assembly, distribution/docs sync, generated byte/mode checks passed. Cache integration compilation failed in newly authored test digest formatting. Codex memory test had Python syntax failure. Custom home install failed in materialized source. Legacy research merge fixture was rejected. Mini six production scenarios passed then missing-project fixture failed. Full docs failed on an excluded Markdown link. Mini site built but crawler claimed handoff absent despite authored content.

The bounded fixes delivered afterward have not run: digest encoding, fixture project/tools, extra parenthesis, guide links, private staging and diagnostic retention. Entity import index/contract071b versus parent HEAD provenance mismatch remains real within test candidate preparation. Cortex2.0.3 real package is missing; absence/disabled path proof does not establish positive integration. Research legacy fixture hardcodes IDs while production checks package-scoped content IDs. Read-only inspection of scripts/verify-protected-tests.mjs:31-38 shows protection applies to BDD feature/steps/support paths, not this shell scenario or JSON fixtures. Fixing these stale fixture identities needs no invented protected-test approval; preserve all behavioral assertions.

Freeze: no further product or harness changes in this analysis child. Preserve all candidate worktrees and original dirty roots. No destructive reset, new features, new test architecture, dependency search/upgrade, real-home mutation, Cargo, or gate execution here.
